name: 5 mm graph paper
headline:
A little order.
A lot of possibilities.
description: Free printable 5 mm graph paper in A4 and US Letter. Download a vector PDF with a 50 mm calibration ruler, or customize the grid.
intro: Five-millimeter squares, a little breathing room, and nothing between you and your next idea. Download a ready-made sheet for math, measured sketches or planning.
uses: Plan a room or garden using your own scale
Arrange a cross-stitch motif on square cells
noteTitle: Millimeters and inches are different grids.
note: Each square is 5 mm wide and 5 mm high: two squares equal 1 cm. A 5 mm grid is not a quarter-inch grid (6.35 mm). Check your worksheet or project requirements before printing.
faq: How many 5 mm squares fit in one centimeter?
Two squares in either direction. Each square is 0.5 cm wide, so a 2 × 2 block covers 1 square centimeter.
Yes. Every fifth line is slightly heavier, marking 25 mm intervals. You can turn this off in the custom generator.
Can I use it as an architectural drawing?
You can choose a drawing scale yourself, but this is blank graph paper, not a certified measurement or drafting document. Check the printed calibration line first.

name: 5 mm dot grid paper
headline:
Less on the page.
More room for you.
description: Download free printable 5 mm dot grid paper in A4 or US Letter. A clean vector PDF for journals, notes and layouts, with a print calibration ruler.
intro: A soft grid of dots that keeps your notes in line without taking over the page. Start a journal, map a week, or give an idea room to grow.
uses: Lay out weekly notes and journal spreads
Sketch diagrams without continuous grid lines
Keep handwriting and hand lettering aligned
noteTitle: The dots guide you. The layout is yours.
note: The dots are 5 mm apart horizontally and vertically, measured center to center. Downloads are blank: they do not include calendars, headings or example handwriting. Change the spacing or dot color in the generator.
faq: Is this a ready-made journal planner?
It is a blank dotted sheet, not a dated planner. Draw your own boxes, headings and trackers using the dots as guides.
Does the PDF contain raster dots?
No. The dots are vector shapes, so the PDF stays crisp when viewed or printed. Print at 100% to preserve the 5 mm spacing.
Can I print a smaller notebook insert?
The ready-made files are A4 and US Letter. Scaling to a smaller size changes the dot spacing too. These templates do not provide automatic notebook imposition.

name: Knitting graph paper
short: See the shape of a stitch.
headline:
Ideas, one little
stitch at a time.
description: Free printable knitting graph paper with 5 × 3.75 mm rectangular cells. Download A4 or US Letter PDFs, or adjust the row-to-stitch ratio for your gauge.
intro: Stitches are not always square. A rectangular grid helps you sketch colorwork with a more useful sense of proportion. Start with our 0.75 ratio, then adjust it to your swatch.
uses: Sketch colorwork motifs on rectangular cells
Compare a motif's proportions before knitting
Map a simple repeat, one cell per stitch
noteTitle: Match your swatch, not a universal ratio.
note: The ready-made sheet uses a row-height / stitch-width ratio of 0.75. For a blocked swatch with 20 stitches and 28 rows over the same distance, use 20 ÷ 28 ≈ 0.714. Enter that ratio in the generator; the default sheet does not automatically match your yarn or stitch pattern.
faq: A knitted stitch is often wider than one row is tall. Rectangular cells can make a colorwork sketch resemble the finished fabric more closely, provided the ratio matches the blocked gauge.
Each cell is 5 mm wide and 3.75 mm high. The height is 0.75 times the width. This is a charting aid, not the physical size of your knitted stitch.
Does the PDF include the sample motif?
No. Downloads are blank grids. The small colorwork example in the sharing image illustrates a possible use; it is not an included knitting pattern.
